Let me analyze the proof obligation carefully:

- **Goal**: `spec.and(always(c)).entails(p.leads_to(q))`
- This means: for all executions `ex`, if `spec.and(always(c)).satisfied_by(ex)`, then `p.leads_to(q).satisfied_by(ex)`
- Which means: `always(p.implies(eventually(q))).satisfied_by(ex)`
- **Given**: `spec.entails(p.and(c).leads_to(q))` — for all executions `ex`, if `spec.satisfied_by(ex)`, then `p.and(c).leads_to(q).satisfied_by(ex)`

The proof strategy:
1. Fix an execution `ex` where `spec.and(always(c))` holds
2. From `spec` holding, get `p.and(c).leads_to(q)` holds on `ex` (i.e., `always(p.and(c).implies(eventually(q)))`)
3. Need to show for all `i`, `p.implies(eventually(q)).satisfied_by(ex.suffix(i))`
4. Fix `i`, suppose `p.satisfied_by(ex.suffix(i))`
5. Since `always(c).satisfied_by(ex)`, we get `always(c).satisfied_by(ex.suffix(i))` (using `always_propagate_forwards`)
6. So `c.satisfied_by(ex.suffix(i))`
7. Thus `p.and(c).satisfied_by(ex.suffix(i))`
8. From `p.and(c).leads_to(q)` at `ex`, get `p.and(c).implies(eventually(q)).satisfied_by(ex.suffix(i))`
9. Apply implies: `eventually(q).satisfied_by(ex.suffix(i))`
